messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: paging: runtime/high-p99 detected spike for service=runtime-hosted-us-east-1. Auto-created INC-2026-048. Root ts=1805550000

alice: I'm on it — seeing p99 ~2.4s (baseline ~250ms). Throughput down ~30% on canary pool. Dash: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/abcd/runtime-p99?orgId=1

ben: I see a stream of kernel selector fallbacks on the canary nodes, lots of 'fallback_to_generic_kernel' entries. Attaching quick log excerpt.

ben: ```
2026-04-12T21:12:05Z kernel_selector: selected=generic_fallback reason=thrash
2026-04-12T21:12:05Z kv_cache: evicted=1249 cause=pressure
2026-04-12T21:12:06Z batcher: microbatch_size=1 window_ms=3
```

carla: Any deploys/flag flips in the last 20m?

alice: We started a staged rollout ~15m ago: release=rev-2026-04-12-2, and flipped feature flag adaptive_batch_v2=true in canary at ~1805549985.

dinesh: That flag enables dynamic microbatch packing + aggressive windowing. I'm seeing a pattern: traffic profile -> many tiny microbatches -> kernel selector jitter -> fallback to slower generic kernels -> KV cache churn. Microbatch jitter correlates with p99 spikes.

eva: Customer impact? Which customers are affected and severity?

alice: So far 3 customers have reported elevated latency for embedding/generation calls (p99 > 3s). No widespread 5xx errors. Support notified.

ben: Recommendation: flip adaptive_batch_v2 off for canary immediately and pause rollout. If latency doesn't improve within 10m, rollback release.

alice: Flipping flag now -> `/ff toggle adaptive_batch_v2 off --scope=canary`

incident-bot: feature-flag change recorded: adaptive_batch_v2 set to OFF by alice at 1805550120

alice: p99 decreased to ~380ms within 90s, throughput climbing back to -5% from -30%. Good signal.

carla: I'll prepare to stop the rollout and coordinate rollback if needed. Ben, can you stage the rollback job for the rest of the wave?

ben: Staging rollback: `/deploy rollback runtime-service --to=rev-2026-04-12-1 --wave=remaining` ready.

alice: Initiating rollback of wave-7 -> started now.

incident-bot: deploy rollback started by alice at 1805550300 (job id: deploy-9876)

dinesh: Kernel fallback counts are dropping, KV eviction rate down 80% since flag flip. We'll watch for re-eviction. Keep monitoring window for 15m.

frank: Product: can we draft a short note for affected customers? I can review.

eva: Draft: "We observed elevated inference latency between 21:12–21:30 UTC due to a canary rollout of a batching optimization. We reverted the change and are monitoring; if you continue to see issues please contact support." Thoughts?

alice: LGTM. Sending to the 3 affected accounts.

carla: Handing off to night oncall — I'm taking this from alice at 1805550600. alice, please stay for 10m overlap if possible.

alice: Ack, I'll monitor for the overlap. Runbook link: https://confluence.redwood.local/rb/runtime-batch-jitter

incident-bot: INC-2026-048 status: mitigated -> partial_recovery (observed baseline restored for canary, monitoring continues). last_update=1805551800

carla: Preliminary RCA: adaptive_batch_v2 packing thresholds were too aggressive for the canary traffic mix, producing many microbatches of size 1. Kernel selector oscillation then chose generic fallback kernels and evicted KV caches, causing increased p99 and reduced throughput.

alice: Next actions: 1) ensure rollout paused for all regions 2) revert flag across environments 3) add min_microbatch_size safeguard + conservative default window for canary profile 4) postmortem and reminder to add canary traffic simulation tests.

ben: I'll open the rollback/guard PR with a config patch to set min_microbatch_size=4 and add a metric-bound gate.

carla: I'll draft the postmortem and schedule a follow-up with infra/release to add rollout stop conditions.

frank: We'll prepare a short exec note and customer outreach plan.

alice: Thanks team. Closing the active paging shift — oncall handoff complete.
